title: Machine-learning species delimitation identifies second species of Micrognathozoa
summary: Transcriptomes plus machine-learning delimitation split the Crozet population as Limnognathia desmeti sp. nov. (Proc R Soc B, 19 Feb 2025).
account: Micrognathozoa, the most recently discovered animal phylum, contained a single species, Limnognathia maerski, known from Greenland, the Pyrenees and a Subantarctic island. Specimens were collected at Pointe du Bougainville on Île de la Possession, Crozet Archipelago, on 10–11 December 2019 (collection funded by a French Polar Institute project awarded to co-author David Renault). Sato and colleagues at the University of Copenhagen, Harvard University, the Natural History Museum London and partner institutions generated transcriptomes from single specimens and tested species hypotheses with standard approaches and with unsupervised (PCA, random forest, t-SNE, VAE) and supervised (delimitR, CLADES) machine-learning methods; the authors preferred the most conservative estimate across PTP, VAE and custom CLADES, which delimits only the Crozet population. The analyzes delimited the Subantarctic population as a new species, Limnognathia desmeti sp. nov., while not definitively separating the Greenland and Pyrenees populations. The paper was published in Proceedings of the Royal Society B on 19 February 2025.
purpose: Test species hypotheses within Micrognathozoa using transcriptomic data and machine-learning species delimitation.
system: Machine-learning species delimitation on single-specimen transcriptomes: unsupervised clustering (PCA, random forest, t-SNE, variational autoencoder) and supervised classifiers (delimitR, CLADES)
deployer: University of Copenhagen Marine Biological Section and co-author institutions
location: Pointe du Bougainville, Île de la Possession, Crozet Archipelago (Subantarctic)
taxonomy_note: Candidate f asked for machine learning on images or audio; here the ML ran on genomic (transcriptomic) data with field-collected specimens, so the fit to the candidate description is loose.

ratings.reason: A verified discrete result for the research team: formal description of a new species in a phylum with one previously known species.
Adds a named taxon and a Subantarctic record to museum and university collections; no operational change documented.
Knowledge gain about a rare phylum's diversity and dispersal; no conservation action or beneficiary population is documented.

ai_role.statement: The paper's title credits machine learning with the identification. Each machine-learning method run (unsupervised PCA, random forest, t-SNE and VAE; supervised delimitR and CLADES) separated the Crozet population, and the adopted two-species result rests on the authors' most conservative estimate across PTP, VAE and custom CLADES, not on delimitR's three-species model, which would also have split Greenland from the Pyrenees. The paper's conclusion also rests on deep phylogenetic divergence, extreme geographical separation and differences in COI and 18S rRNA sequences, so the machine-learning output was one of several lines of evidence rather than the sole basis.
